newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India slides as local sentiment wanes.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India slides as local sentiment wanes.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) slid in lacklustre trade after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram failed to deliver much to stimulate investors in his budget speech on Friday.
"There is nothing so far to get anyone going," said a trader.

The James Capel Indian GDR Index fell 1.16 points, or 1.58 percent to 72.38 points, a premium of 12.29 percent over the local market after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30 share index fell 39.78 points to 3,468.29.
The finance minister will announce further proposals this week, but traders said that they have given up expecting radical changes on minimum corporate tax.
"India has been a bit of a disaster since the election, we had expected a lot but have seen nothing," said a trader.

Indian GDRs are down about 15 percent in the past three months and two new issues from State Bank of India and VSNL, India's overseas telephone monopoly, look set to soak up any excess demand for stock.
"It is fairly easy to take any would-be buyers out of this market when someone starts selling," said a trader.
Bajaj Auto fell 50 cents to $36.00/$37.00 and East India Hotels 92 cents to $20.25/$21.25, while Indian Hotels was down 79 cents to $25.00/$26.00.
Depositary Receipts in other Asian markets rallied after last week's falls.
The Capel Taiwan Index rose 1.97 points 2.22 percent to 90.74 points, a premium of 3.76 percent over the local market, after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 63.46 points or 1.00 percent to 6,435.43.

The Capel Korea Index rose 1.37 points, 2.09 percent, to 66.91 points, a premium of 23.22 percent over the local market, after the Korea Composite Index added 12.12 points, or 1.54 percent, to a provisional close of 797.38.
